sections.title: Which mood after "maybe"?
sections.content: You know *quizás* and *dudo que* with the subjunctive from B1 Unit 13, and *tal vez*, *puede que* and *probablemente* from B1 Unit 22. At B2 the question is how sure you want to sound. The mood after a word for 'maybe' shows it: the indicative makes your guess sound fairly likely, and the subjunctive leaves more room for doubt. One marker, *a lo mejor*, gives you no choice: it takes only the indicative.

sections.title: Markers and the mood after them
rows: A lo mejor takes only the indicative. There is no subjunctive version.
Quizás and tal vez + indicative: you think it is quite likely.
Quizás and tal vez + subjunctive: you are less sure.
Puede que and es posible que always take the subjunctive.
After the verb, quizás and tal vez take the indicative.

items.spanish: A lo mejor Marta se quedó dormida.
Tal vez tenga razón, pero no estoy seguro.
items.english: Perhaps she is right, but I am not sure.

items.spanish: Está en la oficina, tal vez.
items.english: He is in the office, perhaps.

sections.content: *Quizás* allows both moods, but *a lo mejor* does not: *A lo mejor venga* is a typical learner mistake. If you want the subjunctive, switch to *quizás*, *tal vez* or *puede que*. The indicative after *quizás* is not wrong, it only sounds surer.
